open_issues.impact: a host that configured token_ttl above 300 fails config validation at boot
open_issues.text: hub.token_ttl is now capped at 300 seconds (it was 1..3600), not only given a new default. D26 bounds the exposure of a lost control message by exp <= 5 min; with a larger ttl the documented bound token_ttl + clock_skew would not hold. The doctor message and the tests changed accordingly; hub.clock_skew is validated as 0..60.

open_issues.text: Detail choices made at implementation level (D44): (1) JWT claims node/drive/epoch/mode were renamed to document_id/drive_id/generation/scope (read|write); tenant, schema_version, room and iat stay, permissions_version {drive, global} and jti are added. iat/exp and the verification use the application clock (Carbon; JWT::$timestamp/$leeway are set around decode and restored). (2) The event's reason is the causing event type, or the host's word for AccessInvalidation (pattern /^[a-z][a-z0-9_.:-]{0,63}$/). Its subject is access with id drive:<id> or global. The event property is named reach because DomainEvent::scope() already exists; the payload key stays scope. (3) A folder gives scope subtree, a file or document node; drive deletion records drive scope with reason drive.deleted at the transition to deleting, and the purge records no further invalidation. (4) Transport failure: log + metric, the delivery finishes done, no retry. (5) The control consumer drops a change older than token_ttl + clock_skew. The relay resumes a paused consumer from reconciled_through_seq, so a re-enabled module would otherwise replay old messages. (6) A replayed occurrence of the event increments the version once more (the sink answers Skipped, like GenerationCloser); this only adds one extra recheck. (7) Recheck answers reason token|gone|generation|unavailable|revoked and jti per connection; at most 200 per call. (8) A new Api value DriveRef::of(DriveSnapshot|DriveHandle|int|string), since no DriveRef existed.

open_issues.impact: a naming or type detail may differ on a real engine
open_issues.text: The pgsql and mysql expected snapshots (96 files) gained v_collaboration_permission_versions by hand, from the patterns of existing tables (character varying(191)/varchar(191) PK, bigint counter with <table>_version_check / <table>_chk_1, timestamp(0)/timestamp updated_at); no engine ran (D41). The sqlite files were written by scripts/schema-snapshot.sh.

For P5.11 (hub): (a) the JWT carries drive_id, jti, scope read|write, permissions_version {drive, global} and exp = iat + 300; the backend accepts exp up to hub.clock_skew (30 s) past it, but the hub's local check in index.js (decodeTokenExpiry, exp*1000 <= now) has no skew yet. (b) POST /v1/collaboration/hub/renew: body {room}, bearer = current token, signed and with protocol 2 like every room call. Answer {token, room, generation, scope, mode, exp, jti, permissions_version}; 403 without View (close), 404 gone, 409 epoch mismatch. (c) POST /v1/collaboration/hub/recheck: signature only (like compaction), body {connections: [{id, token}]} with 1..200 entries, answer {results: [{id, access none|read|write, reason, jti}]} in order. (d) Control message JSON {v:1, drive_id|null, scope node|subtree|drive|global, permissions_version (the drive's or the global version now), at (ISO ms Z)}. Redis transport: PUBLISH on vaulter:collab:control. HTTP transport: POST <url>/control for each control.http.urls entry, headers X-Vaulter-Collab-Timestamp/X-Vaulter-Collab-Signature = hex HMAC-SHA256 of '{ts}.{rawBody}' with hub.webhook_secret; any non-2xx counts as a failure. The management listener defaults to 127.0.0.1, so the HTTP transport needs a reachable MANAGEMENT_HOST. (e) The append ack adds permissions_stale (bool); renew at once when true. (f) Until P5.11 renews, sessions close as token-expired every 300 s by default and clients re-open them.

open_issues.impact: performance and concurrency are unverified on server engines (D41)
open_issues.text: Residual risks for review: (1) every permission change of a drive row-locks drive:<id> in v_collaboration_permission_versions until its transaction commits, and host global invalidations share one row; lock order is the journal head lock (main event) first, then the version row; the append path only reads versions. (2) While the collaboration module is off, no versions are counted and no control rows exist. This is harmless because append and renew always check rights and old tokens expire within 300 s. (3) recheck opens each room in turn (one access check per connection, up to 200 per call).

summary: Drive: new event Vaulter\Drive\Events\Access\EffectivePermissionsChanged (type drive.access.effective_permissions_changed, DriveEventType case appended at the end; data {drive_id|null, scope node|subtree|drive|global, node_id|null, reason}; subject access drive:<id>|global; activity false, external false, journal null) recorded in the transaction of grant create/revoke, inheritance change, share create/update/rotate/revoke, node move/trash/restore/purge, drive archive/unarchive and the transition to deleting (reason = the causing event type). New enum InvalidationScope, Api DriveRef::of(snapshot|handle|id) and Api AccessInvalidation::changed(?DriveRef, reason) (OperationRunner, operation drive.access.invalidate, system actor whose reason is the host's; null = global). Collaboration: migration 000504 + CollaborationSchema entity collaboration_permission_versions (scope_key varchar(191) PK, version counter, updated_at; no FK); EventSink collaboration.permissions (PermissionVersionSink) increments drive:<id>/global in the event transaction (UPDATE +1, else insertOnce, else UPDATE). Room tokens minted by new RoomTokens with claims sub, document_id, drive_id, tenant, generation, schema_version, scope read|write, permissions_version {drive, global}, room, iat, exp = iat + token_ttl (application clock), jti; the resolver verifies with hub.clock_skew leeway. Config: hub.token_ttl 300 (1..300), hub.clock_skew 30 (0..60), control.transport redis|http|none (default none), control.redis.connection, control.http.urls, control.http.timeout; validated at boot and in the doctor. HubRoom/open() mark tokens older than the current versions as stale; append always re-checks rights and its ack adds permissions_stale. New POST /v1/collaboration/hub/renew (room token + signature: rights checked now, new exp/jti/versions, write->read without Edit, 403 without View, 404 gone, 409 past generation) and POST /v1/collaboration/hub/recheck (signature only, up to 200 {id, token}: results {id, access none|read|write, reason, jti} in order). Ephemeral OutboxConsumer collaboration.control publishes {v:1, drive_id, scope, permissions_version (current), at} through ControlTransport: Redis PUBLISH vaulter:collab:control, HTTP POST <url>/control signed like hub calls (X-Vaulter-Collab-Timestamp/Signature, HMAC of {ts}.{body} with the webhook secret), or none; a failure is logged and counted (vaulter_collab_control_failures_total) and the delivery finishes as done; a change older than token_ttl + clock_skew is dropped (vaulter_collab_control_stale_total). Tests: drive tests/Access/EffectivePermissionsChangedTest.php (13); collaboration tests/Revocation/{PermissionVersionsTest, RenewTest, AppendRevokedTest, EffectivePermissionsTest, ControlConsumerTest} (45) with support classes tests/Support/{Revocation, RecordingControlTransport}; existing tests adjusted for the claim rename, the new event and routes.
